title: Unprecedented: France records 5,764 excess deaths during heatwave
facts: France recorded 5,764 excess deaths among people aged 15 and older during a summer heatwave.
French public health agency Santé Publique France monitored mortality data between June 17 and July 2.
The 5,764 excess deaths represent the highest heatwave-period mortality figure in France since 2003.
The 2003 European heatwave caused approximately 15,000 deaths in France.
France recorded 5,722 heat-related excess deaths between June and mid-September of the previous year.
Approximately two-thirds of the excess deaths recorded in France occurred among individuals aged 75 or older.
Less than 20% of the excess deaths in France were among individuals aged 45 to 64.
Half of the 5,764 excess deaths occurred across a three-day span from June 25 to June 27.
France experienced its hottest month of June since nationwide meteorological recording began in 1947.
Temperatures exceeded 40 degrees Celsius in numerous locations across France during the heatwave.
The average temperatures recorded in France on June 24 and June 25, 2026, were the highest in the country's history for any month.
Santé Publique France noted that the excess deaths were attributed to all causes pending specific heat correlation.
French health authorities characterized the excess mortality rate during the heatwave as unprecedented.
The recorded heatwave episode in France spanned from mid-June to early July 2026.
The heatwave mortality surge concentrated heavily within the final week of June 2026.
